masked.business_two_sentences: This is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing an oral, once-daily drug that activates a liver-specific hormone-receptor pathway to treat a chronic fatty-liver disease and a related inherited cholesterol disorder. It has no approved products and no product revenue as of the most recent quarter.

transparent.business_two_sentences: Madrigal Pharmaceuticals is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing MGL-3196 (resmetirom), an oral, once-daily thyroid hormone receptor-beta agonist, for non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) and heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH). The company has no FDA-approved products and reported zero product revenue through the third quarter of 2018.

what_changed.fact: The company presented 36-week Phase 2 biopsy and lipid results for its lead drug at a hepatology-conference plenary session; topline results were already public by 13 Mar 2018 (week 12) and 31 May 2018 (week 36) [c1][c2][c3].
what_changed.relationship_to_business: This is the company's only late-stage clinical program; the depth of this data underpins the planned Phase 3 trial and the company's near-term value [c1].

what_changed.fact: Q3 results showed $488.5 million in cash and investments (up from $191.5 million a year earlier), zero product revenue, and guidance for a Phase 3 trial in the primary indication to start late 2018 or early 2019, pending regulatory agreement on design [c4][c5][c6].
what_changed.relationship_to_business: Sets the financing backdrop: management called its resources significant relative to the planned Phase 3 programs, but regulatory agreement on the pivotal trial design was not yet public [c7][c12].

what_changed.fact: In June 2018 the company completed an underwritten public stock offering, issuing 983,607 new company shares, with net proceeds of about $282.8 million for general corporate purposes including R&D and trial costs [c8].
what_changed.relationship_to_business: This financing, not the November data, is the main driver of the large cash increase and the roughly 8% share-count increase seen in the numbers above [c8][c9].

programs.indication: Non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH): a fatty-liver disease in which fat buildup causes liver inflammation and cell damage, and which can progress toward cirrhosis.
programs.drug_mechanism: An oral, once-daily small-molecule drug that selectively activates the thyroid hormone receptor-beta (a liver-cell receptor that helps regulate fat and cholesterol metabolism).
programs.phase: Phase 2 completed (week-12 and week-36 data reported); Phase 3 planned
programs.ownership_partner: Wholly owned by the company; no partner disclosed in the eligible sources
programs.design: Randomized 2:1 (drug:placebo), double-blind, placebo-controlled, multi-center, about 25 U.S. sites [c13]

sample_sizes.note: exact planned-vs-enrolled distinction not separately stated in the eligible sources [c13]

programs.treatment_duration: 36 weeks, with an optional 36-week extension for some patients
programs.primary_endpoint: Relative reduction in liver fat content at week 12, measured by MRI-PDFF (a non-invasive MRI method that estimates the fraction of fat in the liver)
programs.secondary_endpoints: Liver fat reduction sustained to week 36; NASH resolution on liver biopsy; a >2-point improvement in the NAFLD Activity Score (a biopsy-based severity score); fibrosis change; normalization of the liver enzyme ALT; lipid changes

latest_evidence.week12_primary: 36.3% liver-fat reduction overall (42.0% in a pre-specified high-exposure subgroup) vs 9.6% for placebo, p<0.0001 [c14]
latest_evidence.fibrosis: Resolved in 50% of drug-treated patients who achieved NASH resolution; >=1-point reduction in 29% of drug-treated vs 23% of placebo patients [c16]
latest_evidence.ALT: Significantly more normalization in drug-treated than placebo patients [c17]
latest_evidence.safety: Mostly mild-to-moderate adverse events, balanced between arms; mild loose stools at treatment start in the drug arm [c18]
latest_evidence.missing: No confidence intervals were stated in the eligible sources for the percentage effect sizes above; only p-values were given.

programs.management_says_vs_regulator_says: Management said the NASH-resolution result 'suggests a high likelihood of success' in a similarly designed, longer Phase 3 trial and described NASH resolution as 'an approvable FDA endpoint' [c12]. No independent regulator statement is in the eligible packet; the company itself said the Phase 3 design was still 'pending regulatory agreement' as of the cutoff [c12].
programs.next_milestone: Planned start of a Phase 3 trial, guided for late 2018 or early 2019, subject to regulatory agreement on design; announced 2018-11-06 [c6]
programs.economic_relevance: Pre-revenue; this is the company's primary value driver. The company said its cash position was significant relative to its currently planned Phase 3 programs, but gave no specific trial-cost figure [c7].

programs.indication: Heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH): an inherited condition causing very high LDL ('bad') cholesterol from birth.
programs.drug_mechanism: The same thyroid hormone receptor-beta agonist drug as the NASH program, tested for its cholesterol-lowering effect.
programs.ownership_partner: Wholly owned by the company; no partner disclosed
programs.trial_id: missing -- not stated in the eligible sources
programs.design: missing -- described only as a completed Phase 2 clinical trial; randomization ratio and blinding not separately confirmed in the eligible sources
programs.treatment_duration: missing -- not stated in the eligible sources
programs.primary_endpoint: missing -- not explicitly labeled in the eligible sources, though LDL-cholesterol lowering is the headline result reported
programs.secondary_endpoints: Other lipid measures were also reported as improved in the same release, without full detail

latest_evidence.LDL_C: 18.8% placebo-corrected reduction, p<0.0001; 21% in an optimal-dose subgroup [c19]
latest_evidence.safety: Not separately detailed for this trial beyond a general 'mild-to-moderate, balanced' characterization applied to the company's Phase 2 program overall
latest_evidence.missing: Confidence intervals, exact patient disposition, and full secondary-endpoint results were not located within the research budget for this program.

programs.management_says_vs_regulator_says: Management said it was evaluating the design and objectives of a possible Phase 3 study in this indication that could begin in 2019; no regulator statement is available [c20].
programs.next_milestone: Possible Phase 3 study, design/objectives still under evaluation as of 2018-11-06; no confirmed start date [c20]
programs.economic_relevance: Secondary to the NASH program in company communications; no separate spending figure disclosed.

sector_evidence.existing_products: none -- the company reported zero product revenue for both the three- and nine-month periods ended 2018-09-30 and has no FDA-approved products [c5]

unresolved_questions: Whether the regulator will agree to the proposed pivotal-trial design for the primary indication, and on what timeline, given that agreement had not been publicly confirmed as of the cutoff.
Whether the week-12 and week-36 imaging- and biopsy-based results from a 125-patient Phase 2 trial will replicate in a larger, longer pivotal trial.
How the company will prioritize and fund development of the second (cholesterol-disorder) indication alongside the primary liver-disease program.

own: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2 trial met its week-12 primary endpoint (liver-fat reduction) with p<0.0001, and the effect was sustained through week 36 [c14][c15].

36-week liver-biopsy data showed statistically significant NASH resolution (27% vs 6.5% placebo, p=0.02) and fibrosis improvement, endpoints management described as approvable by regulators [c3][c16][c12].

The company holds $488.5 million in cash and investments against about 15.4 million shares outstanding and no debt line items found in the structured financial data, which management called significant relative to its planned Phase 3 programs [c4][c9][c21][c7].
flat: Regulatory agreement on the proposed pivotal Phase 3 trial design had not been publicly confirmed as of the cutoff; the company itself described it as 'pending' [c12].

The Phase 2 population was small (125 enrolled; as few as 34 placebo patients had paired week-36 biopsies), so effect sizes in a larger, longer Phase 3 trial are not established by this data alone [c13][c3].
short: The results getting the most attention (NASH resolution, fibrosis change) are secondary, biopsy-based endpoints from a small trial; the company has not secured regulatory agreement on how to run a confirmatory trial, and that trial's cost is not yet disclosed [c3][c12][c7].
Nearly all of the year's large cash increase came from a June 2018 stock sale rather than from operations, and the company is pre-revenue with no approved product [c8][c5].

editorial_notes: The 12 Nov 2018 conference presentation elaborated on (rather than first announced) the trial's efficacy data: the week-12 primary endpoint was already public by 13 Mar 2018 and the week-36 secondary/biopsy results by 31 May 2018 [c2][c3]. The LDL-cholesterol figures (18.8% / 21%) are attributed here to the company's separate, previously completed HeFH trial, based on the clearest available source language (the 13 Mar 2018 and 6 Nov 2018 releases both tie this figure to the 116-patient HeFH trial); the 12 Nov 2018 and 31 May 2018 NASH-trial releases also reference the same lipid figures without fully disambiguating which trial they came from, so a reviewer should double-check this attribution against the original HeFH topline release if it becomes available [c19]. The June 2018 stock offering's per-share price was intentionally omitted from this packet; only share counts and dollar proceeds are shown, per the instruction to keep price data out of the pre-decision bundle. Funding-runway and quarterly-cash-outflow figures are scenario calculations built from a single lumpy nine-month cash-flow total (a large one-time financing swamps the operating trend) and should be read as illustrative, not predictive.
